children: rose 0.43% premarket after Guggenheim initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $365 price target, implying 49% upside. The stock sits near its 52-week low of $244.76, down 30% over six months.

Management changes, a delayed missile initial public offering and general sector uncertainty have weighed on the shares and the multiple. Guggenheim built a value-creation framework contemplating a missile solutions IPO alongside further steps to unlock shareholder value.

The firm expects L3Harris to sustain a book-to-bill ratio above one for the remainder of 2026 and total revenue growth of at least a high single-digit rate, with the product portfolio positioned for defense spending tailwinds running from weapons and missile replenishment through modernization. It also argues the company deserves more credit for a commercial-based defense electronics operating model that has produced operating margins materially above peers.
Jefferies started coverage at Hold with a $315 target, citing the leadership change and the unclear path for the missile IPO.

title: L3Harris Is Down 30% and Guggenheim Calls It a Buy
